svg.title: Each tree is fitted to what is still wrong
svg.desc: Four panels showing the same eight points fitted by a step function that gains one step per boosting stage, with the red vertical residual bars visibly shrinking and the sum of squared errors falling from 163.88 to 41.87 to 16.24 to 11.11, beneath which the Newton leaf-weight formula is written out with the curvature term circled and three lambda values shrinking the leaf from -0.286 to -0.019, and a bar chart where max_depth at 0.0101 dwarfs learning_rate at 0.0006.
svg.text: Each tree is fitted to what is still wrong
each new tree is fitted to the RESIDUALS - the red bars
- not to y. The bars are the only thing it ever sees.
a plain GBM writes 1 where XGBoost
how much each hyperparameter actually moved the score
learning_rate barely matters ONCE EARLY STOPPING IS ON.
It buys you time, not accuracy.
...and how do I explain ONE prediction? -> SHAP, 0.65 ms/row
